summary: Yosemite's first permanent lookout, built by the NPS in 1931 in rustic style; NRHP-listed in 1996 and still standing and reachable as of a 2024 visit.

facts.design: rustic two-story structure: stone first story topped by a wooden cab with catwalk

staffing.status: NPS fire lookout; helitack crews based at the lookout during fire season (1995 nomination)

access.note: reached by a paved road off Big Oak Flat Road and a trail built for visitors; the sources do not say whether the cab interior is open

visit.trail_note: a short trail from the parking lot near the top of the access road, or a longer lower trail from the Tuolumne Grove trailhead (2024 trip report)

events.note: built by the National Park Service as the first permanent lookout in Yosemite, in rustic style
one-story plywood shed addition built to the east
1995 nomination says the shed and lean-to were to be removed and the lookout fully restored; completion not confirmed
added to the National Register of Historic Places on April 4, 1996
registered on the National Historic Lookout Register on June 4, 1998

notes_for_editor: The brief's 1931 build and 1998 NHLR registration are confirmed. NRHP listing (1996) and the 1995 nomination were not in the brief's events and are added. The Wikipedia 'still in use in the 1980s' is a decade, not a year, so no year-specific event was created. The 1995 nomination's planned restoration and helitack use are from the nomination text itself; I found no source confirming the restoration was done. Access is marked public because the trip report and the NRHP nomination describe visitor access to the lookout, but the sources do not confirm whether the cab interior is open to visitors; check before treating that as settled. Staffing as_of is the 1995 nomination date, the only staffing detail found. The Atlas Obscura and Parkwolf listings were seen only in search results and are not cited.
